title: Recursion: a function calling itself

spans.text: Recursion solves a problem by handling a smaller version of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a stopping case; without it, calls continue until a limit is reached. Think of opening nested boxes one at a time.
Each call reduces the number and stops at 0, printing 3, 2, 1.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Find the stopping case first, then trace how each call uses a smaller input. A loop may be safer for very deep input.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Python limits recursion depth; consider an iterative solution for large or user-controlled input.
